summary: Fresh pass 34 screenshot review: modal checklist overlays are largely gone and B20 tab proof was added, but production UX still fails because multiple action/detail screens have low-contrast washed-out panels, repeated generic utility shells, sixteen workflow/persona scorecards block, and six workflows lack persistent lifecycle result proof.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target personas?
visibleEvidence: Some home/tab screens look closer to a modern app, but action/detail screens still include washed-out panels and repeated utility-card layouts.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the experience feel like a rich community product rather than a workflow implementation surface?
visibleEvidence: Affected screenshots include real domain labels, but the repeated action/status shell still dominates the task experience.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Can target users see the full task lifecycle, including alternate actions and persistent result/receiver states?
visibleEvidence: Six lifecycle scorecards still fail persistent result state.

findings.title: Action/detail screens still use low-contrast repeated utility shells
visibleEvidence: Representative after screenshots show readable hero headers but lower action/detail panels that are near-white-on-white or repeated status blocks, including plant exchange, export/import, HOA dues, ad-off, platform safety/ad-status, and soccer privacy/export screens.
findings.description: Pass 34 fixed the modal/dim overlay pattern and added tab evidence, but several action screens are still not visually production-grade: important content is washed out, the repeated panel structure feels like a generic task harness, and the UI does not yet read as purpose-built product surfaces.
findings.requiredFix: Create readable, domain-native action/detail surfaces for the affected workflows. Use opaque surface colors with accessible contrast, screen-specific layout, real domain objects and inputs, explicit primary/secondary/lifecycle actions, and visible result/receiver states; then full recapture B12-B20 evidence.
concreteRequiredFixes: Fix contrast on every affected action/detail panel so text is visibly readable in screenshot pixels.

Replace repeated utility/status card stacks with workflow-specific surfaces such as marketplace listing editor, export wizard, checkout/receipt, announcement composer, roster privacy manager, and messaging/ad-status surfaces.
Keep bottom-tab and persona navigation proof while adding product-specific content and controls.
acceptanceChecks: Zero B25-REPEATED-CARD-SHELL-LIKELY visual rows.
Independent LLM vision screen reviews pass for every affected row.
Production judge has no major/blocker ticket for visual readability or generic action shell.

findings.title: Workflow/persona product experience remains too generic on sixteen workflows
visibleEvidence: The deterministic workflow/persona scorecards still block sixteen workflows. The screenshots show domain words, but the surfaces are often generic action/detail compositions rather than complete persona-native product experiences.
findings.description: The current UI demonstrates improved content density but not yet full product experience depth for affected personas. Several workflows require a richer workflow-specific model rather than the same visual shell with different labels.
findings.requiredFix: For each blocking workflow/persona pair, implement a surface that makes the target persona real job obvious: object context, user inputs/decision data, primary action, alternative/change/reject/cancel path, result/receipt/history, and receiver/continuation state.
